title: “Would You Want an AI Tutor?” Understanding Stakeholder Perceptions of LLM-based Systems in the Classroom
extended_summary:
This paper addresses a gap in the educational AI literature: although large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being used in schools as tutors, teaching assistants, and curriculum-support tools, there is no systematic way to capture the perceptions of the stakeholders affected by these systems. The authors argue that responsible deployment depends not only on technical performance, but also on understanding what different stakeholder groups value, fear, and expect from LLM-based tools in classroom settings.

To address this gap, the paper proposes Co-PALE (Contextualized Perceptions for the Adoption of LLMs in Education), a stakeholder-first framework for eliciting and organizing perceptions of LLM-based systems. The framework considers four dimensions in sequence: stakeholders, context, goals, and perceptions. It is designed to help educational decision-makers identify who is affected, in what educational setting and discipline, for what instructional purpose, and which perceptions should be assessed.

The paper is based on a targeted literature review of 38 articles on perceptions of LLM-based systems in education. The authors found that existing studies are heavily skewed toward students and teachers, mostly in higher education and STEM, while K-12, parents, administrators, and other stakeholders are underrepresented. They conclude that current evidence is fragmented and context-poor, and they present two illustrative K-12 use cases—an elementary AI teaching assistant/tutoring pilot and a high-school curriculum support tool—to show how Co-PALE can be used in practice.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed conceptual/framework paper grounded in a targeted literature review and content analysis, but it is not an empirical effectiveness study and does not use a rigorous comparative design. The authors explicitly note the framework has not yet undergone direct empirical validation.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper likely has modest but indirect impact on K-12 adoption practice by offering a stakeholder engagement framework and identifying concerns such as privacy, fairness, and overreliance. However, it provides no measured outcome improvements, so its demonstrated impact on educational performance or operations is unclear.

interventions.use_case: Stakeholder perceptions of LLM-based classroom systems such as AI tutors and AI teaching assistants, including student-facing tutoring bots and instructor-facing lesson/curriculum support tools.

finding.finding_summary: This paper does not estimate learning effects; it synthesizes stakeholder perceptions and proposes the Co-PALE framework for governing LLM adoption in schools. Across the reviewed literature, perceptions were mixed: students were often positive (56%), while teachers were more often negative (52%), especially around ethical concerns, and the authors emphasize the need for stakeholder engagement before rollout.
finding.measure: Qualitative content analysis of 38 papers on stakeholder perceptions; framework development and illustrative case mappings
